From the middle of the 16th century, the names of chess players who have been widely regarded as the strongest of their time have been passed down. stories.title: First Thing: Blockbuster Anthropic IPO fails to halt global slide in AI stocks
stories.summary: Record-breaking IPO for company behind Claude comes amid tumbling prices for other AI stocks. Plus why the humble potato could be vital for future space missions Good morning. Global stock markets have slumped as Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a sell-off in AI-linked companies. The sell-off followed losses on Wall Street on Thursday, where the main indices all fell by over 2% on a day dominated by Anthropic’s IPO. The blockbuster debut easily places Anthropic’s IPO as the biggest in history, with the 980m shares sold raising $81bn, surpassing the previous record. According to reports, demand for Anthropic shares was about six times what the company was able to offer. US economic growth is inextricably tied to the booming AI sector, and in particular the vast investments in datacentres that power programmes such as Claude and ChatGPT. Who has been made wealthy by Anthropic’s IPO ? Dan Milmo and Aisha Down profile the seven co-founders of the company who are now worth $180bn – with physicists, a former journalist and an associate of the pope among the company’s guiding lights. How has the White House responded to the recent spate of tech failures? The White House national ⁠cyber director, Sean ⁠Cairncross, ​has been ousted from his job , days after tech outages hit US air travel, banking and national security systems. The Department of Defense chief information officer, ​Kirsten Davies, will ‌assume the position ‌temporarily. How have the scattered communities of Rohingya reacted to the judg ment? There were tears in the halls of The Hague in the Netherlands and an eruption of applause in the refugee camps of Bangladesh. Farida Khatun, 50, who has been a refugee in Bangladesh since 2017, said : “Since we arrived here, we have been waiting and looking forward to this justice”. But she does not expect to be able to return home; her village was completely destroyed by Myanmar’s forces and no longer exists. Continue reading...

Researchers with Just Safe, a victims’ advocacy non-profit, found that 84% of people who had been incarcerated reported being assaulted, shot or stabbed before their first time in jail or prison. The report is based on a nationally representative survey of 20,000 Americans. stories.title: Don’t blame cyber-attacks for recent outages. The real villain is the US economy | Bruce Schneier
stories.summary: Our tech infrastructure is riddled with problems. But they’re all downstream of the incentives baked into shareholder capitalism It’s been a bad week for our computerized infrastructure. We’ve seen outages at Microsoft , the FAA , a handful of banks , United Airlines , an unnamed classified NSA network , and Apple . People should be forgiven for suspecting a coordinated cyber-attack, a common cause, or at least a conspiracy. But there is none. The incidents are unrelated. They’re not the result of any cyber-attack, coordinated or not. And, even more surprising, they don’t seem to be the result of AI. (We can’t say anything about the NSA; we’ll probably never know the details of that one.) It’s really just a series of unfortunate coincidences. Continue reading...

stories.title: AI is imposing a hidden ‘cognitive tax’ on the lowest-paid workers
stories.summary: It’s time to rethink welfare as AI reshapes the economy and wears down the brains of some of the most vulnerable workers AI is adding to the cognitive load of workers already stretched thin by unpredictable pay, insecure housing and mounting debt – and the lowest paid feel it most. We need to rethink welfare for an economy being reshaped by AI. Throughout the history of the study of economics, the human brain, which directs our labour, judgment and resilience, has rarely been considered an asset in its own right. The emerging AI economy is changing that. As machines take on routine work, what becomes most valuable is the judgment, creativity and insights only people can provide. Economists coined a term for this in recent years: brain capital. Markets & Economy.summary: Record-breaking IPO for company behind Claude comes amid tumbling prices for other AI stocks. Plus why the humble potato could be vital for future space missions Good morning. Global stock markets have slumped as Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a sell-off in AI-linked companies. The sell-off followed losses on Wall Street on Thursday, where the main indices all fell by over 2% on a day dominated by Anthropic’s IPO. The blockbuster debut easily places Anthropic’s IPO as the biggest in history, with the 980m shares sold raising $81bn, surpassing the previous record. According to reports, demand for Anthropic shares was about six times what the company was able to offer. US economic growth is inextricably tied to the booming AI sector, and in particular the vast investments in datacentres that power programmes such as Claude and ChatGPT. Who has been made wealthy by Anthropic’s IPO ? Dan Milmo and Aisha Down profile the seven co-founders of the company who are now worth $180bn – with physicists, a former journalist and an associate of the pope among the company’s guiding lights. How has the White House responded to the recent spate of tech failures? The White House national ⁠cyber director, Sean ⁠Cairncross, ​has been ousted from his job , days after tech outages hit US air travel, banking and national security systems. The Department of Defense chief information officer, ​Kirsten Davies, will ‌assume the position ‌temporarily. How have the scattered communities of Rohingya reacted to the judg ment? There were tears in the halls of The Hague in the Netherlands and an eruption of applause in the refugee camps of Bangladesh. Farida Khatun, 50, who has been a refugee in Bangladesh since 2017, said : “Since we arrived here, we have been waiting and looking forward to this justice”. But she does not expect to be able to return home; her village was completely destroyed by Myanmar’s forces and no longer exists. Continue reading...

We’ve seen outages at Microsoft , the FAA , a handful of banks , United Airlines , an unnamed classified NSA network , and Apple . People should be forgiven for suspecting a coordinated cyber-attack, a common cause, or at least a conspiracy. But there is none. The incidents are unrelated. They’re not the result of any cyber-attack, coordinated or not. And, even more surprising, they don’t seem to be the result of AI. Markets & Economy.summary: It’s time to rethink welfare as AI reshapes the economy and wears down the brains of some of the most vulnerable workers AI is adding to the cognitive load of workers already stretched thin by unpredictable pay, insecure housing and mounting debt – and the lowest paid feel it most. We need to rethink welfare for an economy being reshaped by AI. Throughout the history of the study of economics, the human brain, which directs our labour, judgment and resilience, has rarely been considered an asset in its own right. The emerging AI economy is changing that. As machines take on routine work, what becomes most valuable is the judgment, creativity and insights only people can provide.
